name: Leaky Vessels runc/containerd container escape (CVE-2024-21626)
command: docker run -w /proc/self/fd/<n> <image>   # runc leaked-fd cwd escape to host
description: CVE-2024-21626 (Leaky Vessels) is a container-escape bug in runc <=1.1.11 (used by Docker, containerd, CRI-O, Kubernetes). runc leaks an open file descriptor pointing at the host filesystem (an ancestor of the container's working directory). By setting the container WORKDIR (or process.cwd) to /proc/self/fd/<n>, a process inside the container resolves paths relative to the host root, allowing read/write of host files and full escape to the host as root. A build-time variant abuses the same leak via a crafted Dockerfile WORKDIR.
notes:
=== WHAT IT IS ===
  runc leaves a file descriptor open to the host filesystem when it sets up the
  container. If the container's working directory is set to that leaked fd via
  /proc/self/fd/<n>, the container process operates on the HOST filesystem (outside
  the container root), giving read/write to host files as root -> full escape.

=== AFFECTED ===
  runc <= 1.1.11 (fixed in 1.1.12). Pulls in Docker Engine < 25.0.2 /
  containerd < 1.6.28 / 1.7.13, CRI-O, and Kubernetes nodes using them.
  docker --version ; runc --version ; containerd --version

=== RUNTIME VARIANT (run with attacker-chosen WORKDIR) ===
  # The leaked fd number varies (commonly 7-9). Point cwd at it and read/write host:
  docker run --rm -w /proc/self/fd/8 <image> \
    bash -c 'cat /etc/shadow; echo PWNED > /host_file'
  # Writing to ../../../../etc/cron.d/x or a host SUID path escalates on the host.

=== BUILD VARIANT (malicious Dockerfile) ===
  # In a Dockerfile:  WORKDIR /proc/self/fd/8  then RUN a command that touches the
  # host filesystem during 'docker build'. PoC repos: snyk/leaky-vessels-dynamic-detector,
  # NitroCao/CVE-2024-21626, Wall1e/CVE-2024-21626-POC.

=== PoC REPOS ===
  git clone https://github.com/NitroCao/CVE-2024-21626
  # follow the repo: build the image, run with -w /proc/self/fd/<n>, confirm host access.

=== ALTERNATIVES ===
  cgroup release_agent escape; docker-socket abuse; --privileged container escape

defense.why_it_works: During container setup runc keeps a file descriptor open to a directory on the host filesystem and does not close it before handing control to the container process. Because /proc/self/fd/<n> dereferences to that host directory, a container that sets its working directory (process.cwd) to the leaked fd resolves relative paths against the host root, escaping the container mount namespace with the container's (often root) privileges.
defense.prerequisites: The ability to run a container (or submit an image/Dockerfile to a build) on a host using runc <=1.1.11 / Docker <25.0.2 / containerd <1.6.28 or <1.7.13. No host credentials needed - just control of a container's WORKDIR/cwd or build steps.
defense.impact: Full container-to-host escape with read/write of host files as root, defeating the container boundary - critical in multi-tenant Docker/Kubernetes and CI build environments.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1611] Containers whose working directory or process cwd is set to /proc/self/fd/<n>; container processes accessing host paths via a /proc/self/fd symlink; docker run -w /proc/self/fd/... or a Dockerfile WORKDIR under /proc/self/fd; unexpected host-filesystem writes originating from a container runtime.
defense.artifacts: auditd/EDR records of a container process opening paths under /proc/self/fd that resolve outside the container rootfs; docker/containerd logs showing an unusual WORKDIR; host files modified with a container runtime as the writer; runc debug logs.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=linux (sourcetype="linux:auditd" OR sourcetype=docker)
| search (proctitle="*/proc/self/fd/*" OR ProcessCommandLine="*-w /proc/self/fd/*" OR CONTAINER_WORKDIR="*/proc/self/fd/*")
| table _time, host, exe, proctitle
defense.elastic_kql: process.args:*\/proc\/self\/fd\/* and (process.name:runc or container.runtime:* or process.args:*\-w*)
defense.sentinel_kql:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/self/fd/" and (ProcessCommandLine has "-w " or ProcessCommandLine has "WORKDIR" or InitiatingProcessFileName in ("runc","containerd-shim","dockerd"))
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine
// container cwd set to a leaked host fd (CVE-2024-21626)
defense.prevention: Upgrade runc to 1.1.12+ and the bundled Docker (25.0.2+) / containerd (1.6.28+/1.7.13+) / CRI-O. Scan images and Dockerfiles for WORKDIR under /proc/self/fd; restrict who can run containers or push build jobs; enable runtime detection for /proc/self/fd cwd and host-path access from containers.

detections.name: Container cwd set to leaked host fd (Leaky Vessels)
detections.logic:
DeviceProcessEvents
| where ProcessCommandLine has "/proc/self/fd/"
| where ProcessCommandLine has "-w " or ProcessCommandLine has "WORKDIR" or InitiatingProcessFileName in ("runc","containerd-shim","dockerd")
| project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, ProcessCommandLine
detections.false_positives: Legitimate use of /proc/self/fd as a container working directory is extremely rare.
detections.tuning: Alert on any container WORKDIR/cwd under /proc/self/fd; correlate with host-path file access by a container runtime.
